subject: networks
question: What transport does HTTP/3 run over?
options: Raw IP with no transport layer
explanation: HTTP/3 (RFC 9114) maps HTTP onto QUIC (RFC 9000), which runs over UDP.

subject: networks
question: Which QUIC feature lets a connection survive a client's IP address change, e.g. moving from Wi-Fi to cellular?
options: Connection IDs that are independent of the IP/port 4-tuple
explanation: QUIC identifies connections by connection ID, so packets from a new address can be matched and the path migrated.

subject: networks
question: Which HTTP/1.1 limitation does HTTP/2 stream multiplexing address?
options: TCP-level head-of-line blocking after packet loss
The cost of the TLS handshake
Application-level head-of-line blocking, by interleaving many streams on one connection
explanation: HTTP/2 splits messages into frames on independent streams, so one slow response doesn't block others at the HTTP layer.

subject: networks
question: How does a browser typically learn that a server supports HTTP/3?
options: An ICMP probe to UDP port 443
An Alt-Svc header or HTTPS DNS record advertising h3
The SNI value in the certificate
explanation: Since HTTP/3 uses a different transport, clients discover it via Alt-Svc or SVCB/HTTPS records rather than an in-band Upgrade.

subject: networks
question: Why can HTTP/2 still suffer from head-of-line blocking?
options: HPACK forces requests to be serialized
One lost TCP segment stalls every stream because TCP delivers bytes strictly in order
explanation: All HTTP/2 streams share one TCP byte stream, so a loss holds back data for all of them until it is retransmitted.

subject: networks
question: How does QUIC use TLS?
options: It runs TLS over a TCP connection beneath QUIC
It doesn't use encryption at all
It integrates the TLS 1.3 handshake, carrying its messages in QUIC CRYPTO frames
explanation: RFC 9001 uses TLS 1.3 for keys and authentication while QUIC handles packet protection and transport.

subject: networks
question: Which header compression scheme does HTTP/3 use?
explanation: QPACK (RFC 9204) adapts HPACK so out-of-order delivery across QUIC streams doesn't cause head-of-line blocking.
